request.spec:
The sheet has a list of holidays (a date entry and an add button; HOLIDAY_ADDED date=<date>; a
date already on the list is refused with an error beside the entry). A claim's due-by, when it is
fixed at creation, is moved past any holiday: when the date plus the terms falls on a holiday, the
due-by is the next day that is not a holiday. The holidays on the sheet when the claim is created
decide; a holiday added later leaves existing due-by dates as they are.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet has a list of holidays (a date entry and an add button; HOLIDAY_ADDED date=<date>; a
date already on the list is refused with an error beside the entry). A claim's due-by, when it is
fixed at creation, is moved past any holiday: when the date plus the terms falls on a holiday, the
due-by is the next day that is not a holiday. The holidays on the sheet when the claim is created
decide; a holiday added later leaves existing due-by dates as they are.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Sheets now have a holiday list, and a new claim's due-by skips any holidays on the sheet when the claim is added. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V53__holiday.sql`, adds a `holiday` table with one row per date per sheet. The database itself refuses a duplicate date on the same sheet.
- **Server:** a new `holiday` package lists and adds holidays at `/api/sheets/{id}/holidays`. Adding a date that's already on the list is refused and writes nothing. A successful add writes `HOLIDAY_ADDED sheet=… by=… date=…` to the audit file.
- **Due-by rule:** in `ClaimService`, if the claim's date plus its terms lands on a holiday, the due-by moves to the next day that isn't one. A due-by already stored is never recalculated, so holidays added later don't change existing claims.
- **Front end:** a new Holidays section on the main screen has a date entry, an Add button, the error message next to the entry, and one row per holiday.

**Decision for you:** I applied the same rule when a claim is split, because the split-off part is a new claim whose due-by is set at that moment. The request only mentions claims being created, and the tests don't cover splits, so if splits should keep the plain date-plus-terms due-by, that's a one-line revert.

Two smaller points:
- The holiday list always shows the current holidays, even when you're viewing the sheet "as of" an earlier date.
- The existing guards still block viewers and archived sheets from adding holidays.
